## Shopping Between Business Meetings

We offer your group a six-hour shopping trip around [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) accompanied by an English-speaking guide. We will agree on the shopping destinations and route based on your preferences.

For a corporate program, we arrange transport pickup at Windsor Oceânico. We will schedule departure around the conference and the group's evening plans.

## Petrópolis is a charming, picturesque town known as the "Imperial City"

Petrópolis is a charming city in the Serra do Mar mountains, just 70 kilometers from Rio de Janeiro. Known as the "Imperial City," this picturesque town served as the summer residence of the Brazilian imperial family and has retained the atmosphere of that era. Walking through the streets of Petrópolis, you immerse yourself in the history and architecture of the nineteenth century, when the city was a center of the country's cultural and political life. One of its main attractions is the Imperial Palace, a magnificent neoclassical building where Emperor Pedro II lived. Today, the palace is a museum displaying luxurious interiors, antique household objects and the emperor's personal belongings. Other highlights include the Cathedral of St. Peter, remarkable for its Gothic architecture and refined interior. It is the resting place of Emperor Pedro II and members of his family. Petrópolis is also known for its beautiful gardens and parks. The Crystal Palace is an elegant glass structure surrounded by a picturesque garden that frequently hosts flower exhibitions and cultural events. Visits to chocolate factories and local restaurants, where you can try traditional Brazilian dishes, provide a pleasant addition to your walk. Beyond its historic attractions, Petrópolis offers outdoor activities in the surrounding mountains and forests. It is an excellent destination for hiking, cycling tours and nature observation. A visit to Petrópolis promises a memorable journey into the past amid beautiful nature and rich history.

The full-day excursion starts in Cusco and travels through the Sacred Valley of the Incas.

In Pisac, visit a craft market selling ceramics, wool products, silverwork and leather goods. At the Awanakancha center, see llamas, alpacas, guanacos and vicuñas, and learn about wool processing and dyeing with natural pigments.

In Ollantaytambo, explore an archaeological complex of monumental terraces, stone structures and remains of fortifications. Between stops, enjoy views of Andean valleys; the excursion introduces both Inca heritage and local crafts.

Enjoy a buffet lunch at a restaurant serving national cuisine. Return to Cusco and stay overnight at the Xima Cusco 4★ hotel or a similar property.

The first stop is [Sacsayhuamán](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/), built during the Inca period. According to local legend, people from other tribes were forbidden to enter the complex. It was regarded as a sacred place associated with the house of the Sun.

Next, see Coricancha, also known as the Temple of the Sun. According to legend, the fifteenth-century temple was richly adorned with gold, including its interior walls and an altar shaped like a solar disk.

After the Spanish conquest, the temple was partly destroyed and a monastery was built on the site. A later earthquake damaged the Spanish building and revealed the massive Inca stone walls.

The next stop is Tambomachay, a water temple with an intricate network of channels and pools. According to tradition, the Great Inca came here for ritual bathing.

Nearby stands Puka Pukara, the "Red Fort," an archaeological complex with walls and towers that served a defensive role. In a single day, this program connects several monuments around Cusco and illustrates different types of Inca architecture: military, religious and engineering.
